packageFit.keepOutReason: the observed keep-out of the published point, 658.29 / 5248 (teams/hardware/inputs/physical_design_space.json, reserveFraction option 0.1254: recorded as observed, not chosen). A tighter reserve is an unverified ASSUMPTION there and is deliberately not used here to admit a candidate
packageFit.reason: 8 compute dies at the candidate's die area (shared-port charge included) plus the memory cubes must fit the placement window less the keep-out. The published point leaves 67.17 mm2 (09_PACKAGE_POWER_RAS.md; it left 0.189 mm2 before the shared-port reclaim of ADR-0023), so an option may add at most that room divided by the 8 dies to the die area

vectorOps.evidence: ASSUMPTION (O-006): indexer ReLU + weighted FMA across index heads; threshold/radix top-k select over the scored context; KDA per-channel decay + delta update; KDA matrix FLOPs as k3_operator_sram_sim (7 x B x heads x 128 x 128). Softmax ops per score belong to the expUnit dimension

lowPrecisionInput.evidence: ASSUMPTION (placeholder, HW-02 AI-Core owner to sign off; O-012): a decode stage on the tensor operand path between local SRAM and the BF16 MAC array. Each sub-BF16 element is widened (FP4 E2M1 / FP8 E4M3 -> BF16 mantissa and exponent) right before the MAC; the block scale is not multiplied per element but applied once per block on the partial sum -- as an exponent add for MXFP4 (E8M0 shared scale, 32 weights along K) and as one FP32 multiply per 128 latent dims for FP8 KV (QK: per K block on the accumulator; PV: per output column). Local SRAM keeps the packed bytes; the MAC array stays single-format BF16. The replay is the nativeTensor one (unpack and KV dequant leave the vector lanes); only the area differs. 3% = decoder (about 40 gates per weight-side element, one per MAC on a weight-streaming GEMV) plus one scale adder/multiplier per block against about 1500-2500 gates per BF16 MAC; a derivation, not a macro. The break-even in the document says how far it may be wrong before the premise flips
lowPrecisionInput.requires: Tile IR operand descriptor carries the block size and the scale pointer (MXFP4: 32 along K; FP8 KV: 128 along K for QK, 128 along N for PV); docs/architecture/contracts/ change

expUnit.evidence: ASSUMPTION (O-006): an exp/reciprocal special-function unit shared by the lanes; softmax costs max, sub, exp, sum, rescale = 8 ops per score (k3_operator_sram_sim: 8 x B x nh x len); the SFU costs 10% of the vector area (TECH.vectorLaneArea is taken as ALU only)

lanesPerCoreClass.chosen: one lane count for L and H cores
lanesPerCoreClass.reason: A.physical() and mappedPlan() have a single vectorLanes, so a per-class split cannot be replayed on the detailed model yet. L cores need about 4:1 for B=1 GEMV unpack and H cores 44-100:1, so a split would save area; revisit after the model is extended

tmaDecode.chosen: decode in the tensor engine, on its operand path (inlineDequant) or on the vector lanes
tmaDecode.reason: not modeled: decoding in TMA writes BF16 into local SRAM, 2-4x the bytes of FP8/MXFP4, and the TMA/local write-port model (O-007) does not charge it yet. This objection is to decoding BEFORE local SRAM; inlineDequant decodes after it, so local SRAM keeps the packed bytes and is not affected

batch.reason: the published point is B=1 decode; the GEMV bounds for B up to 16 are reported as sensitivity
